(sec-item-objectuserbody)=
# ObjectUserBody

A body whose equations of motion and whose position, and optionally orientation, at a local position are computed by Python user functions: a user finite element or a user rigid body on existing nodes. As it provides the access functions of a body, the body markers (MarkerBodyPosition, MarkerBodyRigid), SensorBody, the loads on these markers and every connector work on it.

## Interface

- Body markers that can be placed on it: [](#sec-item-markerbodymass), [](#sec-item-markerbodyposition), [](#sec-item-markerbodyrigid), [](#sec-item-markeruser)
- Nodes: see the detailed description

## Parameters

The parameters of the item; in a dictionary, its type is 'UserBody':

| name | type | size | default | description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **name** | String |  | '' | objects's unique name |
| **nodeNumbers** | ArrayNodeIndex |  | [] | (symbol: $\mathbf{n}_n = [n_0,\,\ldots,\,n_n]\tp$) the nodes whose {ref}`ODE2 <ODE2>` coordinates are the coordinates of the body, in this order |
| **parameters** | NumpyVector |  | [] | (symbol: $\pv_{par} \in \Rcal^{n_p}$) the parameters of the body - masses, lengths, stiffnesses -, passed to every user function; their meaning is defined by the user functions, see exudyn.advancedUtilities.ParameterLayout; empty by default |
| **constantMassMatrix** | Bool |  | False | True: the mass matrix does not depend on the coordinates and the time; massMatrixUserFunction is called once, its result is kept and reused - computed again after a change of a parameter of the body or Assemble -, and the solvers treat the mass matrix as constant |
| **massMatrixUserFunction** | ObjectUserBodyMassMatrixUserFunction |  | 0 | (symbol: $\Mm(\qv) \in \Rcal^{n\times n}$) A Python user function which computes the mass matrix; it must be given |
| **massIntegralUserFunction** | ObjectUserBodyMassIntegralUserFunction |  | 0 | (symbol: $\Jm_m = \int_V \rho\, \Jm_{pos}\, dV \in \Rcal^{3\times n}$) A Python user function which computes the mass integral of the position Jacobian; needed for MarkerBodyMass and the loads on it, such as LoadMassProportional (gravity) |
| **centerOfMass** | Vector3D | 3 | [0.,0.,0.] | (symbol: $\pLocB_{COM}$) the local position of the center of mass; where MarkerBodyMass and the loads on it are drawn |
| **forceUserFunction** | ObjectUserBodyForceUserFunction |  | 0 | (symbol: $\fv \in \Rcal^{n}$) A Python user function which computes the generalized forces on the right-hand side; zero if not given |
| **positionUserFunction** | ObjectUserBodyPositionUserFunction |  | 0 | (symbol: $\LU{0}{\pv}(\pLocB, \qv)$) A Python user function which computes the global position of the point at localPosition |
| **positionJacobianUserFunction** | ObjectUserBodyPositionJacobianUserFunction |  | 0 | (symbol: $\Jm_{pos}(\pLocB, \qv) \in \Rcal^{3\times n}$) A Python user function which computes the position Jacobian at localPosition |
| **rotationMatrixUserFunction** | ObjectUserBodyRotationMatrixUserFunction |  | 0 | (symbol: $\LU{0b}{\Rot}(\pLocB, \qv) \in \Rcal^{3\times 3}$) A Python user function which computes the rotation matrix at localPosition; optional, for rigid markers |
| **rotationJacobianUserFunction** | ObjectUserBodyRotationJacobianUserFunction |  | 0 | (symbol: $\Jm_{rot}(\pLocB, \qv) \in \Rcal^{3\times n}$) A Python user function which computes the rotation Jacobian (of the global angular velocity) at localPosition; optional, for rigid markers |
| **outputVariableUserFunction** | ObjectUserBodyOutputVariableUserFunction |  | 0 | A Python user function which computes the output variables at localPosition that the body does not compute itself, e.g. strains, energy, accelerations and UserType0 to UserType3; optional |
| **visualization** | VObjectUserBody |  |  | parameters for visualization of item |

## Visualization parameters

The parameters of `VObjectUserBody`, given as `visualization`:

| name | type | size | default | description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **show** | Bool |  | True | set true, if item is shown in visualization and false if it is not shown |
| **graphicsData** | BodyGraphicsData |  |  | graphics data in the local coordinates of the body - the coordinates of localPosition -, drawn with every point mapped by positionUserFunction in the visualization configuration (#3064) |
| **graphicsDataUserFunction** | ObjectUserBodyGraphicsDataUserFunction |  | 0 | A Python function which returns a list of graphics data in global coordinates, from the coordinates of the visualization configuration; the only drawing of the body |

## Drawing

Drawn as [all bodies](#sec-drawing-objectsbody); its `graphicsData` in local coordinates, every point mapped by the positionUserFunction, and what its `graphicsDataUserFunction` returns, in global coordinates; nothing without them.

## Output variables

Available as `OutputVariableType` in sensors, `Get...Output()` and other functions:

```{tabularcolumns} \Y{0.25}\Y{0.25}\Y{0.5}
```

| output variable | symbol | description |
|---|---|---|
| Position | $\LU{0}{\pv}\cConfig(\pLocB)$ | global position of the point at localPosition, from positionUserFunction |
| Displacement | $\LU{0}{\pv}\cConfig(\pLocB) - \LU{0}{\pv}\cRef(\pLocB)$ | global displacement of the point at localPosition |
| Velocity | $\LU{0}{\vv}\cConfig(\pLocB) = \Jm_{pos}\dot\qv\cConfig$ | global velocity of the point at localPosition |
| RotationMatrix | $\mathrm{vec}(\LU{0b}{\Rot})\cConfig$ | rotation matrix at localPosition, from rotationMatrixUserFunction, row by row |
| AngularVelocity | $\LU{0}{\tomega}\cConfig = \Jm_{rot}\dot\qv\cConfig$ | global angular velocity at localPosition |
| AngularVelocityLocal | $\LU{b}{\tomega}\cConfig = \LU{b0}{\Rot}\LU{0}{\tomega}\cConfig$ | local angular velocity at localPosition |
| Coordinates |  | all {ref}`ODE2 <ODE2>` (displacement) coordinates of the nodes |
| Coordinates_t |  | all {ref}`ODE2 <ODE2>` velocity coordinates |
| KineticEnergy | $T = \frac{1}{2} \dot\qv\tp \Mm\, \dot\qv$ | kinetic energy from the mass matrix of the current state; current configuration only; localPosition must be $[0,0,0]$ |
| DisplacementLocal |  | from outputVariableUserFunction, if it is given |
| VelocityLocal |  | from outputVariableUserFunction, if it is given |
| Acceleration |  | from outputVariableUserFunction, if it is given |
| AccelerationLocal |  | from outputVariableUserFunction, if it is given |
| Rotation |  | from outputVariableUserFunction, if it is given |
| AngularAcceleration |  | from outputVariableUserFunction, if it is given |
| AngularAccelerationLocal |  | from outputVariableUserFunction, if it is given |
| Director1 |  | from outputVariableUserFunction, if it is given |
| Director2 |  | from outputVariableUserFunction, if it is given |
| Director3 |  | from outputVariableUserFunction, if it is given |
| Force |  | from outputVariableUserFunction, if it is given |
| ForceLocal |  | from outputVariableUserFunction, if it is given |
| Torque |  | from outputVariableUserFunction, if it is given |
| TorqueLocal |  | from outputVariableUserFunction, if it is given |
| StrainLocal |  | from outputVariableUserFunction, if it is given |
| StressLocal |  | from outputVariableUserFunction, if it is given |
| CurvatureLocal |  | from outputVariableUserFunction, if it is given |
| PotentialEnergy |  | from outputVariableUserFunction, if it is given |
| UserType0 |  | from outputVariableUserFunction, if it is given |
| UserType1 |  | from outputVariableUserFunction, if it is given |
| UserType2 |  | from outputVariableUserFunction, if it is given |
| UserType3 |  | from outputVariableUserFunction, if it is given |

(description-objectuserbody)=
## Detailed description

### Coordinates

The object coordinates $\qv \in \Rcal^n$ are the {ref}`ODE2 <ODE2>` coordinates of its nodes, in the order of
`nodeNumbers`. Every user function gets the reference coordinates $\qv\cRef$ (`qRef`), the total coordinates
$\qv_{tot} = \qv\cRef + \qv$ (`qTotal`, reference plus displacement coordinates) and the velocities $\dot\qv$
(`q_t`) of the configuration asked for, and the parameters $\pv_{par}$ of the body (#3056, #3062): a rigid body
computes with $\qv_{tot}$, a finite element with the displacements $\qv_{tot} - \qv\cRef$ and its reference
geometry from $\qv\cRef$; a function may write `q = qTotal` to keep its expressions short. All of them are
read-only numpy arrays, the local position as well.

### Parameters

`parameters` is a vector of any length - masses, lengths, stiffnesses, also flags and indices as numbers -, whose
meaning the user functions define; `exudyn.advancedUtilities.ParameterLayout` maps it to a dict of named
quantities and back. One recorded symbolic user function then serves every body of its kind, each with its own
parameters, and `SetObjectParameter(body, 'parameters', ...)` acts without recording again. A value that changes
the structure of the computation - a number of integration points, the size of a matrix, a Python `if` - cannot
come from the parameters of a symbolic function, as they have no value while it is recorded; it stays a constant of
the Python code.

### Equations of motion

$$
\Mm(\qv)\, \ddot\qv = \fv(t, \qv, \dot\qv) + \fv_{loads} \, ,
$$

with $\Mm$ from `massMatrixUserFunction` - called once and kept with `constantMassMatrix` (#3058) - and $\fv$ from `forceUserFunction` (zero without it). The
Jacobian of the left-hand side is computed numerically, as for every item without an analytic one.

### Mass-proportional loads

With `massIntegralUserFunction`, the body provides the mass integral of the position Jacobian,
$\Jm_m = \int_V \rho\, \Jm_{pos}\, dV$, so that MarkerBodyMass works on it and LoadMassProportional applies the
generalized force $\Jm_m\tp \bv$ of a load per unit mass $\bv$ (#3063); the marker and the load are drawn at
`centerOfMass`. For a rigid body with mass $m$ and center of mass $\pLocB_{COM}$ it is $m$ times the position
Jacobian at $\pLocB_{COM}$, for a finite element the integral of the shape functions times $\rho$.

### Interface of the body

| function | gives | needed for |
|---|---|---|
| `positionUserFunction` | $\LU{0}{\pv}(\pLocB, \qv)$ | positions of markers, sensors and the drawing |
| `positionJacobianUserFunction` | $\Jm_{pos}(\pLocB, \qv) = \partial \LU{0}{\pv} / \partial \qv$ | MarkerBodyPosition, MarkerBodyRigid: forces into the coordinates |
| `rotationMatrixUserFunction` | $\LU{0b}{\Rot}(\pLocB, \qv)$ | MarkerBodyRigid, optional |
| `rotationJacobianUserFunction` | $\Jm_{rot}(\pLocB, \qv) = \partial \LU{0}{\tomega} / \partial \dot\qv$ | MarkerBodyRigid: torques, optional |

The velocity is $\LU{0}{\vv} = \Jm_{pos} \dot\qv$, the global angular velocity
$\LU{0}{\tomega} = \Jm_{rot} \dot\qv$ and the local one $\LU{b}{\tomega} = \LU{b0}{\Rot}\LU{0}{\tomega}$; the derivative
of $\Jm_{pos}\tp \fv + \Jm_{rot}\tp \mv$ with respect to $\qv$, which the Jacobians of connectors need, is computed
by central differences of the Jacobian user functions. A marker that needs a function the body is not given
raises when it is evaluated.

### Drawing

`graphicsData` (in VObjectUserBody) is given in the local coordinates of the body, the coordinates of `localPosition`:
for a rigid body its body-fixed frame, for a finite element its element coordinates. Every point of it - the
corners of the triangles, the end points of lines, the centers of spheres, circles and texts - is mapped with
`positionUserFunction` in the visualization configuration, also by a nonlinear map, so that a deformable body is
drawn deformed; the normals of the triangles are computed from the mapped corners, the radii of spheres and circles
are kept (#3064). A symbolic positionUserFunction draws without calling Python. `graphicsDataUserFunction` returns
graphics data in global coordinates for anything else; both are drawn, and `show` switches the body off.

### User output variables

With `outputVariableUserFunction`, the body provides at a local position every output variable it does not compute
itself (#3057): the strains, curvatures, stresses, forces and torques of a user element, its potential energy,
accelerations - the function gets `q_tt` -, directors, and the user types `UserType0` to `UserType3`; the list is
that of the output variables below. The function returns an empty list for a type it does not provide, which
raises when the type is asked for. A symbolic function distinguishes the types with
`esym.IfThenElse(outputVariableType == int(exu.OutputVariableType.StrainLocal), ..., ...)` and returns the same
size for all of them. `exu.special.userTypes.SetName(exu.OutputVariableType.UserType0, 'BendingStrain')` names a
user type, so that sensor files and messages write the name and `exu.OutputVariableType.BendingStrain` is the same
value.

The user functions are called serially, one Python call at a time. A renderer that runs in a thread of its
own may not call Python: the body, the markers on it and the connectors, loads and sensors on them are drawn in
the main thread, together with the graphics user functions (#3003).

**Userfunction**: `massMatrixUserFunction(mbs, t, itemNumber, qRef, qTotal, q_t, parameters)`
A user function, which computes the mass matrix of the body.

| arguments / return | type or size | description |
|---|---|---|
| `mbs` | MainSystem | provides MainSystem mbs to which object belongs |
| `t` | Real | current time in mbs |
| `itemNumber` | Index | integer number $i_N$ of the object in mbs, allowing easy access to all object data via mbs.GetObjectParameter(itemNumber, ...) |
| `qRef` | Vector $\in \Rcal^n$ | the reference coordinates of the nodes, in the order of nodeNumbers |
| `qTotal` | Vector $\in \Rcal^n$ | the total coordinates of the nodes - reference plus displacement coordinates - of the configuration asked for |
| `q_t` | Vector $\in \Rcal^n$ | object velocity coordinates of the configuration asked for |
| `parameters` | Vector $\in \Rcal^{n_p}$ | the parameters of the body, see parameters; empty if not given |
| **return value** | MatrixContainer $\in \Rcal^{n \times n}$ | the mass matrix, as numpy array, list of lists or exu.MatrixContainer |

A Python user function gets its vector and matrix arguments as read-only numpy arrays, valid during the call, see [](#sec-userfunctions).

**Userfunction**: `massIntegralUserFunction(mbs, t, itemNumber, qRef, qTotal, q_t, parameters)`
A user function, which computes the mass integral of the position Jacobian, $\Jm_m = \int_V \rho\, \Jm_{pos} \, dV$, the mass-weighted position Jacobian: the generalized force of a load per unit mass $\bv$ (LoadMassProportional, gravity) is $\Jm_m\tp \bv$.

| arguments / return | type or size | description |
|---|---|---|
| `mbs` | MainSystem | provides MainSystem mbs to which object belongs |
| `t` | Real | current time in mbs |
| `itemNumber` | Index | integer number $i_N$ of the object in mbs |
| `qRef` | Vector $\in \Rcal^n$ | the reference coordinates of the nodes, in the order of nodeNumbers |
| `qTotal` | Vector $\in \Rcal^n$ | the total coordinates of the nodes - reference plus displacement coordinates - of the configuration asked for |
| `q_t` | Vector $\in \Rcal^n$ | object velocity coordinates of the configuration asked for |
| `parameters` | Vector $\in \Rcal^{n_p}$ | the parameters of the body, see parameters; empty if not given |
| **return value** | MatrixContainer $\in \Rcal^{3 \times n}$ | the mass-weighted position Jacobian, as numpy array or list of lists |

A Python user function gets its vector and matrix arguments as read-only numpy arrays, valid during the call, see [](#sec-userfunctions).

**Userfunction**: `forceUserFunction(mbs, t, itemNumber, qRef, qTotal, q_t, parameters)`
A user function, which computes the generalized forces of the body: elastic forces, the quadratic velocity terms of a rigid body, damping; on the right-hand side, $\Mm \ddot\qv = \fv$.

| arguments / return | type or size | description |
|---|---|---|
| `mbs` | MainSystem | provides MainSystem mbs to which object belongs |
| `t` | Real | current time in mbs |
| `itemNumber` | Index | integer number $i_N$ of the object in mbs, allowing easy access to all object data via mbs.GetObjectParameter(itemNumber, ...) |
| `qRef` | Vector $\in \Rcal^n$ | the reference coordinates of the nodes, in the order of nodeNumbers |
| `qTotal` | Vector $\in \Rcal^n$ | the total coordinates of the nodes - reference plus displacement coordinates - of the configuration asked for |
| `q_t` | Vector $\in \Rcal^n$ | object velocity coordinates of the configuration asked for |
| `parameters` | Vector $\in \Rcal^{n_p}$ | the parameters of the body, see parameters; empty if not given |
| **return value** | Vector $\in \Rcal^{n}$ | the generalized force vector |

A Python user function gets its vector and matrix arguments as read-only numpy arrays, valid during the call, see [](#sec-userfunctions).

**Userfunction**: `positionUserFunction(mbs, t, itemNumber, localPosition, qRef, qTotal, q_t, parameters)`
A user function, which computes the global position of the material point at localPosition: the position interface of the body.

| arguments / return | type or size | description |
|---|---|---|
| `mbs` | MainSystem | provides MainSystem mbs to which object belongs |
| `t` | Real | time of the configuration asked for |
| `itemNumber` | Index | integer number $i_N$ of the object in mbs |
| `localPosition` | Vector3D $\in \Rcal^3$ | the local position of the point, in the coordinates the body defines (e.g. body-fixed, or the element coordinates of a finite element) |
| `qRef` | Vector $\in \Rcal^n$ | the reference coordinates of the nodes, in the order of nodeNumbers |
| `qTotal` | Vector $\in \Rcal^n$ | the total coordinates of the nodes - reference plus displacement coordinates - of the configuration asked for |
| `q_t` | Vector $\in \Rcal^n$ | object velocity coordinates of the configuration asked for |
| `parameters` | Vector $\in \Rcal^{n_p}$ | the parameters of the body, see parameters; empty if not given |
| **return value** | Vector3D $\in \Rcal^{3}$ | the global position of the point |

A Python user function gets its vector and matrix arguments as read-only numpy arrays, valid during the call, see [](#sec-userfunctions).

**Userfunction**: `positionJacobianUserFunction(mbs, t, itemNumber, localPosition, qRef, qTotal, q_t, parameters)`
A user function of the interface of the body that returns a matrix at localPosition: the position Jacobian $\Jm_{pos} = \partial \vv / \partial \dot\qv$ (3 x n), the rotation matrix (3 x 3) or the rotation Jacobian $\Jm_{rot} = \partial \LU{0}{\tomega} / \partial \dot\qv$ (3 x n, global angular velocity).

| arguments / return | type or size | description |
|---|---|---|
| `mbs` | MainSystem | provides MainSystem mbs to which object belongs |
| `t` | Real | time of the configuration asked for |
| `itemNumber` | Index | integer number $i_N$ of the object in mbs |
| `localPosition` | Vector3D $\in \Rcal^3$ | the local position of the point |
| `qRef` | Vector $\in \Rcal^n$ | the reference coordinates of the nodes, in the order of nodeNumbers |
| `qTotal` | Vector $\in \Rcal^n$ | the total coordinates of the nodes - reference plus displacement coordinates - of the configuration asked for |
| `q_t` | Vector $\in \Rcal^n$ | object velocity coordinates of the configuration asked for |
| `parameters` | Vector $\in \Rcal^{n_p}$ | the parameters of the body, see parameters; empty if not given |
| **return value** | MatrixContainer | the matrix, as numpy array or list of lists |

A Python user function gets its vector and matrix arguments as read-only numpy arrays, valid during the call, see [](#sec-userfunctions).

**Userfunction**: `rotationMatrixUserFunction(mbs, t, itemNumber, localPosition, qRef, qTotal, q_t, parameters)`
A user function of the interface of the body that returns a matrix at localPosition: the position Jacobian $\Jm_{pos} = \partial \vv / \partial \dot\qv$ (3 x n), the rotation matrix (3 x 3) or the rotation Jacobian $\Jm_{rot} = \partial \LU{0}{\tomega} / \partial \dot\qv$ (3 x n, global angular velocity).

A user function of the interface of the body that returns a matrix at localPosition: the position Jacobian $\Jm_{pos} = \partial \vv / \partial \dot\qv$ (3 x n), the rotation matrix (3 x 3) or the rotation Jacobian $\Jm_{rot} = \partial \LU{0}{\tomega} / \partial \dot\qv$ (3 x n, global angular velocity).

**Userfunction**: `outputVariableUserFunction(mbs, t, itemNumber, outputVariableType, localPosition, qRef, qTotal, q_t, q_tt, parameters)`
A user function, which computes the output variables of the body at localPosition that the body does not compute itself: strains, curvatures, stresses, forces and torques of a user element, its potential energy, accelerations, the user types UserType0 to UserType3 (named with exudyn.special.userTypes.SetName); for a type it does not provide, it returns an empty list. A symbolic function distinguishes the types with esym.IfThenElse(outputVariableType == int(exu.OutputVariableType.StrainLocal), ...) and returns the same size for all of them.

(miniexample-objectuserbody)=
## Mini example


```python
#a mass point as a user body on a NodePoint: M = m*I, the position of every point is qTotal
m = 2
node = mbs.AddNode(NodePoint(referenceCoordinates=[1,0,0]))
def UFmass(mbs, t, itemNumber, qRef, qTotal, q_t, parameters):
    return m*np.eye(3)
def UFposition(mbs, t, itemNumber, localPosition, qRef, qTotal, q_t, parameters):
    return qTotal
def UFpositionJacobian(mbs, t, itemNumber, localPosition, qRef, qTotal, q_t, parameters):
    return np.eye(3)
#a point does not rotate; with these, rigid markers and the rotation outputs work on it
def UFrotationMatrix(mbs, t, itemNumber, localPosition, qRef, qTotal, q_t, parameters):
    return np.eye(3)
def UFrotationJacobian(mbs, t, itemNumber, localPosition, qRef, qTotal, q_t, parameters):
    return np.zeros((3,3))
body = mbs.AddObject(ObjectUserBody(nodeNumbers=[node], massMatrixUserFunction=UFmass,
                                    positionUserFunction=UFposition,
                                    positionJacobianUserFunction=UFpositionJacobian,
                                    rotationMatrixUserFunction=UFrotationMatrix,
                                    rotationJacobianUserFunction=UFrotationJacobian))
marker = mbs.AddMarker(MarkerBodyPosition(bodyNumber=body))
mbs.AddLoad(LoadForceVector(markerNumber=marker, loadVector=[0,-m*9.81,0]))

mbs.Assemble()
mbs.SolveDynamic()

#free fall: y = -g/2*t^2 at t=1
exu.sys['testResult'] = mbs.GetObjectOutputBody(body, exu.OutputVariableType.Position, localPosition=[0,0,0])[1] #-4.905
```
